reading.title: Dinner at Grandma's
reading.text: Every Friday my family has dinner at my grandmother's house. She never buys fast food or frozen food. Instead, she goes food shopping at the market and chooses fresh vegetables. Her home-cooked food is delicious, but sometimes it is too spicy for my little brother. Last month my cousin got food poisoning after eating at a street stall, so Grandma says we should always be careful. After dinner we play cards and she tells us stories about her childhood.

I bought fresh vegetables and some rice. Boy: Is the rice spicy? Girl: No, it is not. Boy: Perfect. Home-cooked food always tastes better than junk food.

reading.title: A Hot Day
reading.text: Last Sunday was very hot, so we went to the park with a bag full of drinks. My father had brought bottles of drinking water, and my mother made cold lemonade. I wanted a fizzy drink, but there was a drinks machine only near the gate. My sister said that sugary drinks do not help when you are thirsty. So I had a long cold drink of water instead, and I felt better at once. In the evening we drank up the rest of the lemonade and went home.

reading.title: Sunday Lunch
reading.text: On Sundays, my grandfather cooks a big meal for the whole family. The main dish is usually plov, a traditional dish of our region. There are also two or three side dishes, such as salad and pickles. After the meal, everyone helps to wash the dishes. Last week, however, we went for a meal out because Grandfather was tired. We had a light meal in a small restaurant. He said that the plov there was good, but not as good as his own.

reading.title: Healthy Habits
reading.text: Our school nurse, Mrs Aliyeva, gave a talk about diets. She explained that you do not need to go on a diet to be healthy. A balanced diet with fresh food is enough. She also told us not to eat sweets before dinner because they spoil your appetite. Some students have a healthy appetite after sports, and that is normal. Mrs Aliyeva said that if you lose your appetite for several days, you should see a doctor. At the end, she gave us a list of tips.

reading.title: A Surprise for Mum
reading.text: Last Saturday we organised a surprise party for my mother's birthday. First, I invited her friends and our neighbours. My sister made some party food, including a big chocolate cake. We hid in the living room until Mum came home from work. When she opened the door, everyone shouted, "Happy birthday!" She was so surprised that she laughed and cried at the same time. We played a few party games, and my uncle, who is always the life of the party, told funny stories. It was a perfect evening.
